newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Creditanstalt plans to expand in Hungary.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt plans to expand in Hungary.

text.p: The Hungarian banking arm of Austria's Creditanstalt-Bankverein said on Thursday it boosted its assets, market share and profits this year and plans to continue expansion.
"It will take a few more years, but we are advancing quickly to be among the largest banks (in Hungary)," Creditanstalt Rt Managing Director Matthias Kunsch told a news conference.
Creditanstalt had assets of 106 billion forints at the end of August, up 37 percent from December 31 last year.
The bank reached this growth without weakening the quality of its loan portfolio, Kunsch said, adding that it had reduced its loss provisions since last year.
The bank posted a pre-tax profit of two billion forints in the January-August period, compared to 2.4 billion in the whole of 1995.

Creditanstalt Rt has boosted its market share in Hungary to some three percent from 2.2 percent in 1995. Its market share in corporate foreign currency lending is some around six percent and over 10 percent in corporate foreign currency deposits.
Kunsch said Creditanstalt Rt expected its assets to reach 110-120 billion forints and its pre-tax profit some three billion forints by the end of this year.
Creditanstalt Rt has been expanding rapidly since it was founded in 1993 and it plans to increase its market share in line with widening its network.
Kunsch said the bank would increase the number of its branches to 13 this year from the current nine, and would open seven more branches next year.
The expansion of Creditanstalt Rt may receive a boost if the bank can buy state-owned Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB), the fifth largest bank of Hungary with 1995 assets of some 246 billion forints.
The state privatisation agency APV offered a controlling stake in MHB to strategic investors this week. Bids must be submitted by the end of October 17.
The Creditanstalt group is interested in the sale, but it has not decided yet if Creditanstalt Rt or the Vienna-based Creditanstalt-Bankverein will bid for MHB, Kunsch said.
Creditanstalt is quoted by the press and Hungarian officials as having good chances to win the tender.
